subject: Business Models
title: The Attention Recession
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Attention Recession.

hook.text: Humans have a fixed amount of attention: 16 waking hours. Every new app competes for the same finite resource.

buildup.text: TikTok, Netflix, gaming, podcasts, and AI chatbots all compete for attention that cannot expand beyond 24 hours.

discovery.text: Average screen time is 7 hours/day. Almost no attention left to capture. Growth must come from stealing share.

twist.text: AI that summarizes, automates, and filters may return attention to users. The next model might sell attention back.

climax.text: The attention economy is hitting its ceiling. Future business models must create value without consuming more time.

punchline.text: 7 hours of screen time, no room left. Next models sell time back, not take it.

quiz.question: What is the 'attention recession'?
options: People are less interested in media
Finite human attention is fully saturated with no room for new apps to grow

details.summary: The attention recession describes the growing scarcity of consumer attention as content volume explodes while human attention bandwidth remains fixed..
details.whyItMatters: When attention supply cannot grow but content supply is unlimited, the economics of attention-based businesses change fundamentally..
takeaways: Content supply is exploding while human attention capacity remains constant
Customer acquisition costs rise as attention becomes harder to capture
Only the most compelling content and experiences cut through increasing noise

faq.question: How is the attention recession affecting digital businesses?
faq.answer: Social media engagement per post is declining. Email open rates have dropped steadily for a decade. Ad costs rise as attention becomes scarcer. Content marketing requires dramatically more content to generate the same results. Customer acquisition costs have more than doubled in five years.

faq.question: What strategies help businesses compete in an attention recession?
faq.answer: Building owned audiences through email lists and communities rather than renting attention through ads. Creating fewer, higher-quality pieces rather than more content. Focusing on niche audiences where competition for attention is lower..
